title: GitHub backend: map, tickets, questions, answers, discussions, decisions, domain labels, atomic assignment, map-done on close and merge
summary: Fills the issues half of the GitHub store through gh: the map issue, tickets as sub-issues with kind and domain labels, questions, marked answer, discussion and decision comments, the claim rule, and close and merge returning mapDone; 140 tests against a fake gh.
friction: Two of the fixes after a first APPROVED were real data-loss bugs (a refused reassign dropped the owner; leading-space '### ' text corrupted the map body), found only by the second and third fresh reviews; a backend that writes free text into structured bodies needs its write-path checks reviewed adversarially in round one
lessons_learned: Validate the exact text that will be written (after trim and normalisation), never the raw input: a check before .trim() let a section heading into the map body

deferred.what: Two laptops changing the map body at the same moment can lose one settled line, because GitHub has no conditional write for issue bodies
deferred.why: Needs a new mechanism outside this story

deferred.what: Ticket create and merge make several gh calls in a row; a failure halfway leaves an issue without its sub-issue or blocker link and nothing is rolled back
deferred.why: A retry or repair step is beyond this story

deferred.what: One hand-damaged ticket (a second kind label, an edited section, a damaged marked comment) makes listTickets refuse for the whole project, emptying the map and ticket screens, and makes closeTicket/mergeTicket report failure after the issue is already closed
deferred.why: Skip-or-flag for damaged tickets is a design decision for the screen stories; the runbook warns of it
